title: Evidence list endpoint (GET /api/evidence) meets P50/P95/P99 latency budget under populated-field load
description: listEvidence (evidence.controller.js:114-119) runs Evidence.find(filter).sort().skip().limit().populate('category').populate('subCategory') on every page, repeated at :538-540, :616-618 and :1004-1010 for the org/project/assigned variants. Each populate is an extra round trip per page, so latency should be budgeted against a realistic organization with 10k+ evidence documents, not an empty dev DB.
preconditions: Organization seeded with 10,000+ Evidence documents across 20+ categories/subCategories
Load test tool (k6/artillery) configured against staging vibrantix-backend
steps: Run 50 concurrent virtual users issuing GET /api/evidence?page=1&limit=20 for 5 minutes
Repeat against getEvidenceByProjectId and getMyAssignedEvidence variants
Collect P50/P95/P99 response time from the load test report
expectedResult: P50 <= 200ms, P95 <= 600ms, P99 <= 1200ms for all three endpoint variants. Any variant exceeding budget is flagged with the specific populate() call contributing the most added latency (compare against a populate-free control run).

title: Findings Register table does not DOM-blow when an audit has 1000+ findings
description: FindingsRegisterTab.jsx:423-430 renders <CustomTable data={findings} .../> with no pagination prop. CustomTable.jsx defaults pagination=false (line 36) and at line 126/437 returns/renders the full sortedData array when pagination is false. auditAssuranceService.getFindings(auditId, params) (auditAssuranceService.js:591-592) has no default limit, so the client fetches and renders every finding for the audit in one unpaginated, unvirtualized pass (~8 columns per row per findingsColumns). No virtualization library (react-window/react-virtual/tanstack-virtual) exists in package.json.
preconditions: An audit seeded with 1,200 AuditNonConformance/Finding records
Chrome DevTools Performance panel or Playwright + CDP tracing available
steps: Navigate to /audit-assurance-2/[auditId] and open the Findings Register tab
Record DOM node count, main-thread long tasks, and Time-to-Interactive during initial render
Scroll through the full list and record scripting/rendering time per frame
expectedResult: Current known behavior: all 1,200 rows mount as real DOM nodes (no windowing), producing a measurable long task on initial render. Document the actual TTI/long-task numbers as a baseline and flag for remediation (add pagination or a virtualization library) if TTI exceeds 3s or any single long task exceeds 200ms.

title: Executive dashboard KPI cache serves stale data for up to 60s after underlying risk/vendor/compliance writes, with no active invalidation path
description: dashboard-cache.js getCache/setCache (lines 42-55) key KPI responses as exec-dash:{orgId}:{endpoint}:{md5(params)} with a 60s setex TTL (EXEC_DASH_CACHE_TTL), used across risk-board.controller.js, vendor-board.controller.js, framework-board.controller.js, compliance-board.controller.js, audit-board.controller.js and resource-board.controller.js (60+ call sites). clearCache() is defined (lines 58-65) but a repo-wide search finds zero call sites — no write path invalidates a KPI cache entry when the underlying risk/vendor/compliance record changes.
preconditions: Org with an active risk-board KPI query cached from a prior request
steps: Call GET /api/executive-dashboard/risk-board to warm the cache
Immediately create/close a Risk that changes the KPI's underlying count
Re-call GET /api/executive-dashboard/risk-board within 5 seconds of the write
Wait until >60s have elapsed since the original cache warm and call it again
expectedResult: Current known behavior: the immediate re-call within 5 seconds returns the stale pre-write KPI value (cache hit, no invalidation). The call after TTL expiry returns the correct updated value. This stale-read window should be flagged as a gap requiring write-path invalidation via the existing but unused clearCache().

title: evidence-risk-notify queue (concurrency=1) becomes a serialization bottleneck under burst evidence uploads
description: vibrantix-connector-service's evidence pipeline (src/queues/index.ts:23-45) chains evidence-ingest (conc=5) -> evidence-validate (conc=10) -> evidence-normalize (conc=10) -> evidence-deduplicate (conc=10) -> evidence-store (conc=5) -> evidence-map (conc=10) -> evidence-risk-notify (conc=1, maxRetries=2). The final stage's concurrency of 1 (wired in pipeline.worker.ts:1670) means every evidence item funnels through a single-worker queue regardless of how parallel the upstream stages are.
preconditions: BullMQ + Redis available in a load-test environment
Bulk upload of 500 evidence files queued in a burst
steps: Trigger a batch upload of 500 evidence files within a 60-second window
Record per-queue waiting/active/completed counts every 5 seconds via queue.getWaitingCount()/getActiveCount() for all 9 queues
Compare end-to-end time-to-risk-notification against the time-to-store for the same batch
expectedResult: evidence-store/evidence-map queues drain at their configured concurrency, but evidence-risk-notify's waiting count grows and drains strictly one job at a time, becoming the long pole for end-to-end completion. Document the observed throughput ceiling (jobs/minute) for evidence-risk-notify and flag if it causes the full pipeline's P95 completion time to exceed the 5-minute batch-processing budget.

title: Risk list queries have no local Mongoose schema or explicit index coverage in vibrantix-backend and trigger the slow-query monitor at scale
description: There is no Mongoose model for Risk in vibrantix-backend; the risks collection is accessed only via the raw driver (mongoose.connection.collection('risks')) in dashboard-metrics/index.js:75, risk-board.controller.js:12 and executive-intelligence.controller.js:59. No schema-level indexes are declared for this collection in this repo (it depends entirely on out-of-band indexes, if any, plus the default _id index). database.js:20-40 registers a global slowQueryMonitor plugin logging trace.db.slow_query when a query exceeds SLOW_QUERY_THRESHOLD_MS (default 100ms) — this is real infrastructure to assert against.
preconditions: Access to application logs for trace.db.slow_query entries
steps: Run db.risks.getIndexes() against the seeded collection and record the actual index set
Call the risk-board endpoint and dashboard-metrics endpoint filtering/sorting by organizationId + status + createdAt
Grep application logs for trace.db.slow_query entries emitted during the calls
expectedResult: If no compound index exists on {organizationId, status, createdAt} (or equivalent), the query triggers a collection scan and a trace.db.slow_query log line above the 100ms threshold. Document the actual index set found and the query's measured duration; flag missing indexes for remediation.

title: First authenticated page load for a brand-new user (JIT provisioning path) is measurably slower than a returning user's cached path
description: loadPermissions.js's JIT provisioning path (lines 332-386, jitCreateUser) runs Organization.findById + Role.findOne + User.create + a re-findById before the first request can proceed — on top of the unconditional Organization.findById (line 155) that runs on every request regardless of Redis authz-cache hit. A returning user instead hits getAuthzCache (line 175) and skips most of this.
preconditions: A brand-new Keycloak user who has never authenticated against vibrantix-backend before
A returning user with a warm Redis authz cache entry
steps: Measure time-to-first-byte and total time-to-interactive for the new user's very first authenticated request to /dashboard
Measure the same metrics for a returning user's first request in a new session (cache still warm from a prior session)
Compare the two
expectedResult: The JIT-provisioned first login is measurably slower than the warm-cache returning-user path; document the delta in milliseconds. Flag if the new-user cold-start TTFB exceeds 1500ms, as this directly affects first-impression onboarding performance.

title: Socket.IO scan-progress relay has no debounce/batching and can flood project rooms under concurrent multi-project Prowler scans
description: socket.js relays Redis pub/sub scan-progress messages (channel prowler-{env}:scan:progress:{projectId}) directly via io.to(room).emit(event, data) at lines 271 and 299 — one emit per pub/sub message, with no debounce, batching, or rate limit. Under several concurrent cloud scans each publishing frequent progress updates, this is unbounded emit volume per project room.
preconditions: 10+ concurrent Prowler scans running across different projects, each publishing progress updates at high frequency
A test Socket.IO client subscribed to each project:{projectId} room
steps: Simulate 10 concurrent scans each publishing a progress message to Redis every 200ms for 2 minutes
Measure client-side message receipt rate, delivery latency, and any dropped/backlogged messages per room
Measure server CPU/event-loop lag on vibrantix-backend during the burst
expectedResult: Document the observed emit rate per room and any client-side backlog or delayed delivery. Flag if event-loop lag exceeds 50ms sustained, or if any client observes message delivery delayed by more than 2 seconds versus publish time, as evidence that debouncing/batching is needed on the relay path.

title: In-memory entitlement/credit-ledger caches grow unbounded over process lifetime across multi-tenant load
description: ledger.service.js:26 declares a module-level const _balanceCache = new Map() keyed by orgId:org / orgId:project, with TTL-checked entries (line 57) that are only overwritten on next access or explicitly invalidated (lines 109, 134, 147) — never proactively pruned when expired-but-untouched. entitlement/resolver.service.js:32 has the identical pattern (_cache, lines 125/164/197/203/247), cleared only via a full bus.on(TIER_CONFIG_CHANGED, () => _cache.clear()) event or explicit per-key delete — no periodic sweep of stale keys.
preconditions: Load test capable of simulating requests from 5,000+ distinct organizations/projects over a sustained run
Node.js process heap snapshot tooling (--inspect / clinic.js)
steps: Run a sustained 2-hour load test simulating traffic from 5,000 distinct orgId/projectId combinations, each touched once
Take heap snapshots at 0, 1, and 2 hours and measure the retained size of _balanceCache and the entitlement resolver's _cache
Confirm whether Map size grows monotonically with distinct org/project count rather than plateauing
expectedResult: Document the Map sizes at each snapshot. If size grows roughly linearly with distinct orgId/projectId count touched (rather than stabilizing near active-tenant count), flag as an unbounded in-memory cache growth risk requiring a periodic eviction sweep or LRU cap.

title: Audit Assurance pages using plain instead of next/image show measurable LCP/CLS regression versus optimized pages
description: next.config.js:96-98 configures images.formats: ['image/webp','image/avif'] for next/image, but ConfiguredRequirementsContent.jsx and CreateTemplateAuditPage.jsx (both under audit-assurance-2) use plain tags directly, bypassing that optimization and any built-in layout-shift reservation next/image provides.
preconditions: Lighthouse or WebPageTest access against a staging build
Test project with configured requirements/templates populated with real images
steps: Run Lighthouse against /audit-assurance-2/[id]/configured-requirements and the create-template-audit page
Record LCP and CLS scores, noting which element is the LCP candidate
Run the same audit against a comparable page that uses next/image (e.g. evidence-management) as a control
expectedResult: Document LCP/CLS for both plain- pages versus the next/image control page. Flag if LCP exceeds 2.5s or CLS exceeds 0.1 on the plain- pages and the control page performs measurably better, confirming next/image migration would improve these metrics.
